chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who arrives after the people have departed from Arafat. He said: 'If he has respite until he reaches Arafat from its night, then stands at it, then departs and catches the people at al-Mash'ar before they depart, his Hajj is not complete until he reaches Arafat. And if he arrives and Arafat has been missed for him, let him stand at al-Mash'ar al-Haram, for indeed Allah the Exalted has excused His servant, and his Hajj is complete if he catches al-Mash'ar al-Haram before the sunrise and before the people depart. If he does not catch al-Mash'ar al-Haram, then Hajj has been missed for him, so let him make it a separate Umrah, and upon him is Hajj next year.'

key_terms.الْمَشْعَرِ الْحَرَامِ: Al-Mash'ar al-Haram (the Sacred Monument, i.e., Mash'ar Allah)
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat, the essential station of Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who misses the standing at Arafat during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the critical distinction between missing the *wuquf* at Arafat while still catching the crowd at Muzdalifah versus missing it entirely, a key nuance in Shia fiqh regarding Hajj validity. It establishes that if Arafat is missed but Muzdalifah is reached before sunrise, the Hajj is incomplete until Arafat is performed, whereas a total miss requires converting the current pilgrimage to an Umrah and offering a make-up Hajj the following year. This ruling underscores the principle of divine leniency (*al-'udhr*) for those who genuinely miss the pillar due to delay, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise ritual timing and the hierarchy of Hajj's essential components.
